items.difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 2219-2224: the function SubtreeSeq(t), returning the code of the sequence of all subtrees of the tree coded by t, is primitive recursive. The author proof (2229-2261) builds it in layers: it quotes the primitive-recursive immediate-subtree function, defines a level-by-level helper hSubtreeSeq by primitive recursion, proves that concatenating the images of a sequence-valued function over a sequence stays primitive recursive via the auxiliary g_f defined by primitive recursion, and bounds the tree height by the code t itself so that hSubtreeSeq(t, t) lists all subtrees. Chaining the two primitive recursions and the closure-of-concatenation argument is genuine construction work.
